source_text: Among 69 incident HIV cases (22 circumcised, 47 uncircumcised), circumcision conferred a 53% protective efficacy (95% CI: 22–72%; adjusted RR 0.47, 95% CI: 0.28–0.78), with no evidence of behavioral risk compensation—circumcised men reported similar or slightly fewer sexual partners and condom use rates. [17]
